title: Writing Effective Issues — Bugs, Features, and Tasks
learning_objectives: Write a bug report issue with enough context for a reviewer (or future-you) to act on it
Write a feature request issue that captures the user story and acceptance criteria
Write a task issue for technical work with a clear definition of done
Apply labels, milestones, and assignees correctly to each issue type
outline: The three issue types: bug report, feature request, task
Bug report anatomy: steps to reproduce, expected vs. actual behavior, environment
Feature request anatomy: user story, why it matters, acceptance criteria
Task anatomy: what needs doing, definition of done
Writing for future-you: issues you'll understand 3 months from now
Hands-on: Write one bug, one feature, and one task issue for Helm

helm_context.feature: Helm issue backlog with well-structured entries
helm_context.deliverable: Three Helm issues (one bug, one feature, one task) with proper labels and milestone

criteria: Bug issue includes steps to reproduce and expected vs. actual behavior
Feature issue includes a user story and at least 2 acceptance criteria
Task issue has a clear definition of done
All issues have appropriate labels and are assigned to the MVP v1 milestone

resources.title: How to Write Good GitHub Issues

professor_constraints: Use real Helm features for the hands-on: drag-to-schedule task, Google Calendar sync, task list, etc.
Emphasize 'writing for future-you' — these issues will be the roadmap for months of development
The bug report can be hypothetical (a bug that could exist in a task app)
